top_story_title: No network device security news in this window
top_story_summary: The 24-hour collection window produced a single candidate item, and it does not concern network infrastructure. The report covers an actively exploited unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Orkes Conductor, a workflow orchestration platform; Fortinet appears only as the research organisation that reported the exploitation, not as an affected vendor. No firewall, VPN gateway, router, switch, wireless controller, load balancer, management platform or SD-WAN edge device is implicated.
top_actions: No network-device action is required from this cycle's sources.
If you run Orkes Conductor anywhere in the environment, treat it as a separate application-team escalation - it is outside this digest's scope.
Standing check: confirm HTTPS/SSH/API management on firewalls, VPN gateways and controllers is reachable only from the management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Standing check: reconcile your asset inventory's running versions against each vendor's current fixed-release table and queue anything lagging for the next change window.
executive_summary: No network device security news in this window - one item was collected and it is out of scope.
The single item concerns Orkes Conductor, a workflow orchestration platform, not network infrastructure; Fortinet is named only as the reporting researcher.
No new CVEs affecting firewalls, VPN gateways, routers, switches, wireless controllers, load balancers or SD-WAN edge appeared in the sources.
No CISA KEV additions touching network devices in this window.
Nothing has been padded in to fill the edition.
